findings.technicalDetail: The arm acts as a cantilever; bending stress peaks at the inner corner where the fillet radius sets the stress-concentration factor. On v1 (r = 2 mm) the refined-mesh peak is 171 MPa, i.e. SF = 276 / 171 = 1.61. The protocol v1 sweep (run #4) gives SF 1.86 / 2.11 / 2.34 / 2.51 at r = 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 mm. v2 adopts r = 5 mm for margin; the as-built v2 CAD analysed in run #5 gives 118 MPa (SF 2.34), converged within 1.7%. Tip deflection rises from 0.31 to 0.33 mm (still within 0.5 mm).

proposals.title: Fillet radius study: find the smallest inner fillet that meets SF 2.0
proposals.researchQuestion: Which inner fillet radius, with everything else unchanged, brings the peak von Mises under LC-1 to a safety factor of at least 2.0 on a converged mesh?
proposals.motivation: Runs #1 to #3 locate the governing stress at the 2 mm inner fillet and show SF 1.61 on a converged mesh. The fillet radius is the cheapest geometric lever; a sweep tells the customer the trade-off before any CAD change.
proposals.hypothesis: H1: peak von Mises decreases monotonically with fillet radius, and a radius of at most 5 mm gives SF >= 2.0.
proposals.baselineAndControls: Baseline: run #3 (r = 2 mm, 171 MPa). Control: tip deflection must stay within 10% of baseline, confirming only the local stress changes.
proposals.procedure: Parametrise the inner fillet radius on geometry v1 at 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 mm; mesh each at 0.25 mm at the fillet; solve LC-1; record peak von Mises, location, tip deflection and SF.

outcomes.success: H1 holds: SF >= 2.0 at some radius <= 5 mm and the trend is monotonic.
outcomes.failure: No swept radius reaches SF 2.0, or the peak moves elsewhere.
outcomes.inconclusive: Solves fail to converge or results are not monotonic without explanation.

proposals.safetyBoundaries: Analysis only; no physical testing; sandbox with networking disabled; customer CAD is not modified by the lab.
proposals.wouldEstablish: The fillet radius needed for the margin under LC-1 with these assumptions.
proposals.wouldNotEstablish: Fatigue life, behaviour under other load cases, manufacturability, or anything about the as-built part.

protocolHistory.note: Approved as protocol v1. Refined mesh (0.25 mm) at every radius.

proposals.resultSummary: Run #4: SF 1.61 / 1.86 / 2.11 / 2.34 / 2.51 at r = 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 mm; monotonic; 4 mm is the smallest radius meeting 2.0, 5 mm recommended for margin. Run #5 on the as-built v2 confirms 118 MPa (SF 2.34).
followUpSuggestions: Fatigue screening once the load spectrum (iq-E4) is known.
Check the second load case the customer mentioned at intake (side load), which was not analysed.

proposals.title: Fatigue screening of the v2 fillet
proposals.researchQuestion: Does the v2 fillet survive the expected number of LC-1 cycles with margin?
proposals.motivation: The static margin is established; the service life (iq-E4) is unknown and the fillet is a fatigue hot-spot.
proposals.hypothesis: H1: with the stress amplitude from run #5, a stress-life estimate exceeds the required cycles by a factor of 3.
proposals.baselineAndControls: Baseline: static result from run #5. Control: the same estimate on v1 must be worse.
proposals.procedure: Needs a fatigue solver or a customer-side analysis: not runnable here.

outcomes.success: Estimated life exceeds the requirement by 3x.

proposals.wouldEstablish: A screening estimate of fatigue life.

recommendations.title: Increase the inner fillet radius from 2 mm to 5 mm
recommendations.observedIssue: Peak von Mises 171 MPa (SF 1.61) at the 2 mm inner fillet under LC-1 on a converged mesh (run #3); requirement SF >= 2.0.
recommendations.proposedChange: Change the inner fillet radius to 5 mm (4 mm is the minimum meeting 2.0; 5 mm gives margin). No other geometry change.
guidanceReference: Reducing a stress-concentration factor by increasing the fillet radius is standard practice (general guidance; no specific handbook cited in sample data).
recommendations.expectedBenefit: Peak stress falls to about 118 MPa (SF 2.34) with the fillet converged within 1.7%.
tradeOffs: Mass rises from 184 g to 189 g (+2.7%).
Tip deflection rises from 0.31 to 0.33 mm (within the 0.5 mm limit).
Machining: a larger radius cutter is needed (customer to confirm).
applicabilityLimits: LC-1 only; the side-load case mentioned at intake was not analysed.
verificationSteps: Import the revised geometry as v2.
Re-run the static test on the refined mesh (expect SF >= 2.0).
Re-run the convergence study on v2 (expect change below 5%).
Optionally compare a bench strain measurement at a gauge location against the prediction.
